title: Lleucu's Bell and the Quacking Friends
markdown:
In sunny Whistlewick, where fluffy clouds floated by, lived a little white kitten named Lila. She loved napping in the warm sun.

Bertie the beaver loved to build. He built bridges over little streams. Lleucu the badger polished the big village bell until it shone. She loved the noon bell sound the best. BONG! it rang loud and clear at twelve o’clock.

Every day, Lila stretched, Bertie stopped building, and Lleucu rang her bell. Lleucu would smile. It was a perfect sound.

But one bright day, something surprising happened. As Lleucu’s bell went BONG!, a loud “QUACK! QUACK!” answered from the meadow. The village geese were standing in a line, quacking at the sky.

Lleucu blinked. She had never heard geese quack at noon. She tiptoed to look. The geese looked very serious, necks straight, as if noon had written them a letter and they were answering it in goose.

The next day, Lleucu heard a little “QUACK… QUACK…” as she got ready to ring her bell. When her BONG went out, the geese answered, even louder. She wiggled her nose. “Could they be talking to me?” She decided to try something new. She made her next BONG a little softer, like a happy hum.

The geese, as if they understood, made their quacks softer too. A giggle bubbled up. She added a happy little wiggle to her next BONG. The geese answered with happy, bubbly quacks. Soon it was like they were singing together. Lleucu’s deep BONGs danced with the geese’s cheerful quacks, a noon duet nobody had put on the village list.

Lila twitched an ear from her sunny nap. Bertie stopped building, a big happy grin on his face, hammer still in the air as if the bridge could wait for one more verse.

From that day on, the noon sound in Whistlewick was extra special. Lleucu still rang the bell carefully, but she always listened for her feathery friends. The geese were always ready, lined up neatly. Lleucu’s BONGs and the geese’s quacks danced together like best friends. Lila, waking up, would purr, listening. Whistlewick hummed a happy tune.

She logged shine-polish / first-quack / soft-BONG in no clock book, left Bertie his unfinished plank, and let Lila keep the nap that had learned to include geese. Twelve o’clock, when it came, still came on time, and now it came with company.
